title: Pumpkin Spice Oat Waffles
changes_from_base: Mostly oat flour with a little plain flour, blotted pumpkin purée, low-fat yoghurt and oil instead of milk and butter, spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg, cardamom and fresh ginger; no whisked whites.
summary: Warmly spiced oat waffles made with well-drained pumpkin purée, giving a crisp, firm crust around a tender centre.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
rapeseed oil, plus more for brushing

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Set an oven rack in the middle and heat the oven to 93 °C.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 213 g oat flour, 71 g plain flour, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda, ¾ tsp salt, ¼ tsp nutmeg and ¼ tsp cardamom together in a large bowl.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Press the 425 g tin of pumpkin purée between layers of kitchen paper on a tray until the paper is soaked, then tip the dried purée into a medium bowl.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk in 300 ml yoghurt, 2 eggs, 60 ml rapeseed oil, 50 g sugar and 1 tsp grated ginger, then whisk this into the flour mixture until smooth.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Set a wire rack in the tray in the oven, then heat the waffle iron and brush well with oil.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add a scant 240 ml batter to the iron and cook until deep golden with a crisp, firm outside.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve at once, or keep warm on the rack in the oven, brushing the iron with oil before each waffle.

tips: Press the pumpkin firmly between the kitchen paper layers, as removing the extra moisture is what keeps these waffles crisp rather than soft.
Brush the iron well with oil before every waffle so each one releases cleanly.
Keeping finished waffles on a rack in a 93 °C oven stops them going soggy while the rest cook.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the iron. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
